articles.title: England rugby: Shaun Edwards' Red Roses move inspired by mother - Marlie Packer
articles.summary: England back row Marlie Packer says defence coach Shaun Edwards' surprise move into the Red Roses set-up was partly inspired by his late mother Phyllis.
articles.body:
England back row Marlie Packer says defence coach Shaun Edwards' surprise move into the Red Roses set-up was partly inspired by his late mother Phyllis.

Edwards has joined the world champions for the remainder of their autumn campaign after the end of a six-and-a half-year stint with France.

"He told us a little story, telling us why he wanted to be here," said Packer.

"He was saying about his mum not ever being able to have the opportunity to play, and that she would have loved to have done so.

"It was really cool to hear that she thought we were amazing."

Phyllis Edwards worked as a hairdresser in the family's hometown of Wigan, but was a trusted advisor throughout her son's career. She also cared for Edwards' father Jackie after his own career with league side Warrington was ended by a spinal injury at the age of 24.

"Back in the mid-1990s she was the first person to tell me to study rugby union as well as rugby league, because I always wanted to be a coach and I always took notes of what coaches said," said Edwards at the time.

"When rugby union went professional in 1995, I was at the top of the league game, captain of Wigan who were world champions, but she always told me to learn about rugby union."

Edwards' study paid off. After lifting domestic and European titles during his time coaching club side Wasps, he has won a total of seven Six Nations crowns across stints with Wales and France.

"He's got more Six Nations than quite a few of the girls, to be fair to him!" added Packer, who has been part of 10 Grand Slam-winning sides herself since making her England debut in 2008.

"To have that calibre of coach to want to come and work with the Red Roses, just showcases where the women's game is going and what this Red Roses team has done and are doing.

"He's straight talking. He doesn't say too much, but when he does say something, you hear it."

England's winning run was halted on 39 successive Tests last weekend, when Canada held them to a 26-26 draw at Sandy Park.

England take on New Zealand, the Red Roses' closest challengers at the top of the world rankings, at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, before crossing the Atlantic next month for matches against Canada in Ottawa and Toronto, and a Test against the United States.

"We're not happy with the draw, but we didn't lose a match," said Packer.

"It was a really great game of rugby. If you're a neutral that's the kind of rugby that you want to come and watch - you don't know who's going to win, end-to-end scoring, and such a physical, physical game.

"We know we have to build from last week. We're in a Test series against Canada; that's our first game, now we've got two away legs. We know what we have got to put right."

Live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website and app, with accompanying live text commentary

The WXV Global Series - the new event designed to increase the number and competitiveness of Test matches in the autumn for the world's best women - has delivered several superb games.

In addition to England's draw against Canada, last weekend featured France recovering from 19 points down to beat Australia 29-26 and the United States overhauling a 17-point deficit to see off Ireland 40-36 in Dublin.

Australia also came hard at England on the opening weekend of matches, leading 10-5 at half-time in Salford before succumbing to a 48-15 defeat.

"The Red Roses are always pushing that bar higher, then it's for the other teams to raise their game, that's exactly what's happening and that's what we want as players," Packer added.

"The more the game goes professional, the more the unions put money into their women's sides, we're going to see better contests of rugby.

"We're going to see that the Red Roses have it won in the first half. There will have to be 80-minute performances.

"We don't want to turn up and have to have targets within games because we know we're going to win. We want to be in a rugby contest."

The Black Ferns were the last team to beat England, upsetting them in the Women's Rugby World Cup final at Eden Park in November 2022.

They come into Saturday's contest under the leadership of Whitney Hansen, who has won all seven Tests since taking over as head coach in December, including a 36-14 victory over Canada in April in Kansas.

The match against England takes place a day before the one-year anniversary of the Red Roses' Rugby World Cup final triumph in front of a capacity 81,855 Twickenham crowd.

Packer says the focus for the team is forward however.

"That's history now to us," she said. "It's a massive thing - we can celebrate that World Cup, but actually this squad is very different from that World Cup squad.

"We've become Grand Slam champions since then and we're building to perform really well at WXV.

"Come Sunday on the year anniversary though, I expect the WhatsApp group might pop off with a couple of random photos or something!"

A Rugby Football Union report says hosting the World Cup has been the catalyst for a jump in playing numbers in the girls' and women's game.

The number of girls aged six to 12 playing rugby in clubs grew from 18,000 to 26,800 over the course of four years of investment from government totalling £14.6m.

There was also a 38% increase in women playing rugby at targeted universities, while 28% of those qualifying as coaches and match officials were women. That figure had been 9% before the programme's start.

"Today, more women and girls are playing, coaching and officiating rugby than ever before," said Alex Teasdale, the RFU's executive director of the women's game.

"Across England, we have seen communities come together to break down barriers, challenge perceptions and open the door to a new generation of participants."

articles.title: Man of Steel 2026: Brad O'Neill, Adam Keighran and Lachie Miller named on three-player shortlist
articles.summary: The winner of the Man of Steel award will be announced on Tuesday September 29; Jake Connor is the reigning Man of Steel but is not on the shortlist; The play-offs are under way, live on Sky Sports, and continue through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3
articles.body:
A panel made up of five former Man of Steel winners; Ellery Hanley, Sam Tomkins, James Roby, Joe Lydon and Paul Sculthorpe, narrowed down the 12-player list into a final three.

The panel met three times across the season to look at rounds 1-9, 10-18, and 19-27 and came up with a top five for each third.

Players who had made it into a top five across the season were: O'Neill, Keighran, Miller, Jake Connor, Umyla Hanley, Jez Litten, Tyrone May, Brodie Croft, Daryl Clark, Ash Handley, Bevan French, and Jai Field.

Reigning Man of Steel Connor has not made the final shortlist despite a brilliant season for Leeds Rhinos in which he came up with 43 assists, nearly double the amount of any other playmaker in the competition.

Hanley was also included in the panel's top five on two occasions, the only player to achieve such a feat alongside O'Neill and Miller, but is not in the top three.

Keighran was included in the top five from the panel for the final third of the season.

Combative hooker O'Neill has already claimed the Rugby League Writers and Broadcasters Association (RLWBA) Player of the Year award having helped Wigan to the League Leaders' Shield, the Challenge Cup and within 80 minutes of the Grand Final.

With his tough-tackling, pinpoint passing and impressive durability, the 24-year-old has developed into an integral part of Matt Peet's Treble-chasing side.

Australian full-back Miller has been in the Man of Steel conversation since the opening weeks of the season, when he came out on top in the panel's first vote after the opening nine rounds.

No player has made more than the electric Leeds full-back's 166 tackle busts this term and his brilliant running game has lit up plenty of contests for Rhinos, who were long-time league leaders.

Keighran finished the regular campaign with 16 tries and 107 goals, but he has also earned praise for his hard-hitting defence and classy partnership with free-scoring winger Zach Eckersley.

articles.title: Australia vs South Africa: Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus makes 13 changes to starting side for Perth Test after series win over All Blacks
articles.summary: South Africa have made 13 changes to the side that won the three-match series against the All Blacks to take on Australia in Perth; Watch Australia take on South Africa in a one-off Test on Sunday September 27, with kick-off at 10.45am, live on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Only lock Eben Etzebeth and winger Ethan Hooker retained their starting roles from the team that beat the All Blacks 43-28 in Baltimore to seal a 3-1 win in the inaugural Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series.

Etzebeth will extend his record as the most capped Springbok of all time to 147 Test matches.

Props Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Zachary Porthen will join forces with hooker Johan Grobbelaar in a new-look front row, while two-time World Cup-winning fly-half Handre Pollard returns from a calf injury to form a new halves pairing with fit-again scrum-half Herschel Jantjies.

Centre Andre Esterhuizen has been named skipper, making him South Africa's 68th captain.

Lock Franco Mostert will play his first Test since facing Wales last November.

Despite the mass changes, only three players named in the starting lineup have fewer than 10 Test caps - winger Edwill van der Merwe, lock Paul de Villiers and prop Porthen.

"Australia poses a completely different threat to New Zealand in the way they play, so we believe these combinations would be best suited for the challenge that we will face against them," South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus said.

"This is going to be a big challenge against a team that has been playing good rugby, and who have won four of their last five matches, with their other result being a draw against the Pumas in Argentina."

Erasmus had no second thoughts about allowing veteran duo Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende to return home so they could spend time with family.

"They had a heavy workload in the last few months, and they deserve a break," Erasmus said.

Australia head coach Les Kiss is expected to name his side on Friday with reports centre Joseph Suaalii is set to be handed a start on the wing.

articles.title: WXV: Wales' Seren Lockwood out of USA Test with Carys Cox set for return
articles.summary: Scrum-half Seren Lockwood is out of Wales' second WXV Test, against USA, after failing a head injury assessment.
articles.body:
Scrum-half Seren Lockwood has been ruled out of Wales' second WXV Global Series fixture, against USA in Cardiff on Saturday, after failing a head injury assessment.

Lockwood was taken off during the first half of Wales' eight-try victory over South Africa and is now going through World Rugby's return to play protocols.

It is a blow for Wales with Lockwood and Keira Bevan proving a promising half-back partnership in a new-look backline.

Her absence paves the way for Lleucu George to return at 10, with Bevan reverting to her usual position of nine at Cardiff Arms Park.

"It's always sad to see an individual coming off, but the HIA is great to have on board, we're looking after her," said Wales head coach Sean Lynn.

"She's not going to be available this weekend, but I'm super excited to see the half-back combination that we've got this week."

Wales deliver performance of serious promise

Inspired Wales seal stunning win over South Africa

Carys Cox's return to fitness after summer knee surgery gives Lynn another option in the backline, with Cox able to play centre and on the wing.

"Carys has been superb in rehab, she feels fitter, faster and stronger," said Lynn.

"She always brings a smile, she's always confident and I love her athleticism. She will always beat that first defender and the way we are playing now, she's going to get some ball in hand."

Saturday's game at Cardiff Arms Park comes too soon for fellow back Nel Metcalfe, who will not be ready until next month's two-Test tour of Japan.

"Nel is progressing really well with her rehab, we saw her today in some rugby elements, so fingers crossed we will be seeing her in Japan," Lynn added.

articles.title: United Rugby Championship: Ulster's James Hume ruled out of Edinburgh opener
articles.summary: Ulster centre James Hume is ruled out of Ulster's United Rugby Championship season opener against Edinburgh with a hamstring injury.
articles.body:
Ulster head coach Richie Murphy says he expects centre James Hume to be missing for "a number of weeks" after the centre was ruled out of the province's season opener.

Hume suffered a hamstring injury in training this week before Friday's United Rugby Championship opener against Edinburgh at Affidea Stadium (19:45 BST).

His absence will come as a major blow to Murphy, who is already missing midfield options Jude Postlethwaite and Stewart Moore through injury.

Centre David Hawkshaw arrived during the summer.

"James picked up a muscle injury during the week which was an awful pity because he'd put in a huge amount of work and was probably looking the fittest he'd looked in a number of years," Murphy told BBC Sport NI.

"It's disappointing for James and for us as a team.

"But one man goes down, the next man stands up so it'll be an opportunity for someone else."

The Ulster coach added that the 28-year-old could return to action before the conclusion of the series of matches leading up to the break for Ireland's November internationals.

"He'll be out for a number of weeks. It's hard to say at the moment, it's very early in that injury. There's a possibility he'll be back before the end of the block but we're not sure at the moment."

A squad update issued by Ulster Rugby on Wednesday indicated that three other players - Juarno Augustus and summer signings Matthew Devine and Keynan Knox - had participated in team training after overcoming their respective injuries.

articles.title: Henry Pollock: Northampton chief expects more players to work with promoters like Eddie Hearn as he lifts lid on negotiations
articles.summary: Henry Pollock put pen to paper on a new multi-year deal with boyhood club Northampton Saints on Tuesday; he had signed with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency earlier this year
articles.body:
On Tuesday, Pollock put pen to paper on a multi-year extension with his boyhood club , with the England international agreeing a deal worth £400,000 per year.

At just 21, Pollock already has 13 England caps and made five appearances for the British & Irish Lions during last year's tour of Australia.

Pollock's profile continues to grow, with the flanker becoming the first rugby union player to join Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency at the start of the year. Dowson revealed that the boxing promoter "drove as hard a bargain as he possibly could" during negotiations.

Reflecting on Pollock's decision to join Hearn's agency, Dowson said: "I think we'll see more of it.

"I think headlines and social media engagement, and all that, is positive for the game. Fundamentally, I talked to the coaches about this. We want more people watching the game, more people talking about the game and, ideally, most importantly, more people playing the game at loads of different age groups.

"If Henry Pollock and Matchroom are getting some traction with the public, I think we should encourage that, but also take into account that we've got to continue to deliver that in the right way, and I think we have them."

Hearn told The Telegraph that he believes the 21-year-old is worth more than seven figures, predicting Pollock's value will "skyrocket" over the coming years while also arguing that the value of rugby will rise.

Dowson also lifted the lid on the boxing promoter's role in the negotiations, lauding him for helping him grow Pollock's profile, adding that part of the negotiations were handled by a "traditional rugby agent".

"Eddie's been excellent. He's raised the profile of the game," Dowson said.

"He's raised the profile of Henry and he's done what an agent's supposed to do. He's driven as hard a bargain as he possibly could.

"I've got a lot of respect for Eddie and how he goes about his work and some of the stuff he said in the media was really pertinent.

"I think there's elements of the contract which weren't done by Eddie, which were done by his traditional rugby agent.

"There are things from a marketing point of view and the extracurricular stuff that Eddie really looks after Pollock with, which we'll see more of.

"He wasn't necessarily doing every single negotiation from a rugby point of view."

Pollock has explained in the past that he had an open mind to the next steps of his career, but on Tuesday said he was "massively happy to re-sign with Saints".

Some fans had questioned why the negotiations had taken so long to complete, with the flanker's loyalty coming under scrutiny, but Dowson said the process was made easier by Pollock's desire to stay.

"It's still his job, it's still his career. He needs to make sure he's getting the right deal for his aspirations and all those other elements that come with it," Dowson said. "I don't just mean from a financial point of view; I mean from a full, holistic perspective."

"Would there be loyalty in sport if he wasn't offered a contract? Would that be us not being loyal? I think we've got to be careful around that.

"He's playing really well. He's got lots of people talking about rugby. That's great. We wanted to keep him and he wanted to stay. That's a great position for us to start negotiations from, and that's the great thing about sport.

"People can have an opinion around it, but I don't think it was overly dragged out, to be honest, and I don't think it was ever done... there was no animosity in any way from my perspective."
